binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω, equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure μ instance.
hypotheses: X is measurable from Ω to ℝ with its Borel measurable structure.
Let A be the set of t ∈ [0,∞] such that X is measurable, t ≠ 0, t ≠ ∞, ω ↦ exp((X(ω))^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable, and its μ-integral is at most 2. Let q = inf A. Assume q < ∞.
conclusions: The function ω ↦ exp((X(ω))^2/(q.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable.
Its real Bochner integral satisfies ∫ exp((X(ω))^2/(q.toReal)^2) dμ(ω) ≤ 2.
mathematical_definitions: A = {t : ENNReal | Measurable X ∧ t ≠ 0 ∧ t ≠ ∞ ∧ Integrable μ (ω ↦ exp((X(ω))^2/(t.toReal)^2)) ∧ ∫ exp((X(ω))^2/(t.toReal)^2) dμ(ω) ≤ 2}.
q = sInf A in the complete linear order ENNReal = [0,∞].
ENNReal.toReal converts q to a real number before the denominator is squared.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every measurable space Ω, every probability measure μ on Ω, and every measurable real-valued function X, form q as the extended-nonnegative-real infimum of all nonzero finite scales t for which exp(X^2/(t.toReal)^2) is μ-integrable and has μ-integral at most 2. If q is finite (q < ∞), then the same exponential formed using q itself is μ-integrable and its μ-integral is at most 2.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The statement assumes only a measurable space Ω and a probability measure μ; Ω need not be finite-dimensional, topological, or a real vector space.
The function X is real-valued and Borel measurable; no centering, independence, moment, boundedness, or almost-sure finiteness hypothesis beyond its Real codomain is stated.
Admissible t are explicitly required to satisfy t ≠ 0 and t ≠ ∞, but their infimum q is not asserted to be nonzero. Thus q may equal 0 even though every member of A is positive.

Real division is total in Lean. If q = 0, then (q.toReal)^2 = 0 and division by this denominator is defined by the field's zero-inverse convention rather than being undefined; this can make the displayed exponential degenerate rather than express a positive-scale normalization.

The hypothesis q < ∞ excludes q = ∞. In the complete ENNReal lattice, an empty admissible set has infimum ∞, so this hypothesis also rules out the usual empty-set infimum case, though it does not itself provide a named admissible witness.
The conclusion includes integrability separately from the inequality. This matters because the totalized Bochner integral expression exists syntactically even for a nonintegrable function.
No conclusion states q ≠ 0, q ∈ A, or the measurability conjunct at q; only the two analytic conjuncts from admissibility are concluded.
The exact field/constructor content of IsProbabilityMeasure is omitted from the dossier, so the conventional normalization μ(Ω) = 1 cannot be checked solely from the supplied declaration body.
ambiguities: The packet gives only the type, not the constructors or fields, of MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure. Its conventional reading is that μ is a probability measure, but the exact encoded normalization law is not exposed.

The implementation body of MeasureTheory.integral is opaque in the packet (MeasureTheory.wrapped✝.1); its type and surrounding standard structures identify its role as the real-valued Bochner integral, but its nonintegrable-function fallback behavior is not displayed here.
